title: Seller DNA playbook — inference adoption (draft)
content:
One-line summary: A compact, action-first playbook for field sellers and SEs to start and win inference pilots with platform teams.

Audience: Platform engineers, integration SEs, solution architects, and revenue sellers running technical pilots.

Primary goal: shorten pilot time-to-evidence (metrics that matter: p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, request durability) so we can convert to Dedicated or Private commitments.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Prospect already has an ML/infra team but may prefer not to manage inference ops.
- Typical request shapes: 1–2 concurrent realtime routes, plus an embedder batch job.
- Security/regulatory concerns: data residency, audit logs, KMS.

30s pitch (engineer-friendly):
"Redwood gives you the same API for hosted, reserved, and private inference so you can prototype on the hosted tier and flip to dedicated capacity without changing code. We also expose per-token latency and cost telemetry so you can tune for production economics, not just model quality."

Top value props to lead with (order matters):
- Predictable latency at scale: Dedicated pools + autoscale policies with p95 targets.
- Cost controls: batching, KV/prefix caching, and optimized kernels reduce per-token spend.
- Operational safety: model pinning, automatic fallback routes, and traceable audit logs.
- Same integration surface across deployment modes — reduces migration risk.

Quick technical framing for SEs (two-line bullets):
- Runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine with continuous batching and KV-cache aware routing.
- Fallbacks: Route to a quantized variant or lower-throughput model when capacity is constrained; transparently monitored in console.
- Observability: Token-level breakdowns, per-route SLOs, and trace links to request payloads.

3-minute demo script (high-level):
- 0:00–0:30 — Confirm their production goals (latency SLA, cost envelope, data residency).
- 0:30–1:15 — Show API call (simple generation) and Console telemetry (p50/p95, token cost, model version pinned).
- 1:15–2:00 — Flip to a slower quantized variant in the UI and show graceful fallback behavior.
- 2:00–3:00 — Walk through pilot success metrics and ask to schedule sandbox run.

Pilot plan (compact, 6-week cadence):
- Week 0: Kickoff + success criteria (signed MOU + access). Confirm SLIs: p50, p95, cost/1k tokens, 5xx rate.
- Week 1: Sandbox integration (API keys, basic route + model), sample dataset for embed test.
- Week 2: Functional verification and prompt-quality check (SME review of outputs).
- Week 3: Load and latency test (simulate traffic, validate autoscale + fallbacks).
- Week 4: Small production canary (limited traffic, monitor for regressions).
- Week 5–6: Decision period — scale to Dedicated or schedule Private baseline.

Pilot exit criteria (pass/fail):
- Pass: p95 <= target SLA, cost in agreed envelope, no unresolved data residency blockers.
- Fail: consistent output-quality regressions vs baseline or unresolved security/compliance blockers.

Quick objection bank (bite-sized responses for SEs):
1) "We run our models in-house to control cost." -> "Totally fair. For many teams the ops tax and reliability overhead grow faster than model runtime cost; our Dedicated model lets you compare unit economics with and without ops overhead and provides transparent token-level billing for apples-to-apples comparisons."
2) "Latency spikes are our #1 worry." -> "Recommend a canary with pinned model + autoscale; show p95 SLI and circuit-breaker fallback to a slightly cheaper model. Also demo prefix caching for repeated conversational contexts."
3) "We can't send data to an external API." -> "Private deployment or VPC-hosted option; we provide KMS/HSM integrations and can sign addenda for data handling."
4) "Will quantization break output quality?" -> "We run a short A/B on prompt sets; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization targets by workload and flags regressions in our quality monitoring."

Buyer personas and playlets (two-sentence play each):
- Platform Architect: Focus on migration friction. Show the API parity and rollback mechanics. Ask: "What would you be most afraid of if you switched runtime?"
- Head of ML/Model Ops: Focus on unit economics. Run a cost simulation (1k tokens) and highlight caching/batching gains.
- Security/Compliance lead: Focus on auditability and KMS. Offer a private deployment checklist and sample SOC artifact mapping.

Short scripts (copyable):
- SE opener to platform lead: "If we can show p95 within your SLA and a predictable per-request cost in two weeks, would you consider a Dedicated pilot?"
- CFO conversation nugget: "We help you trade compute spend for predictable monthly committed costs and fewer on-call incidents from inference flakiness."

Canary & failure-mode checklist (operational quicklist):
- confirm model version pinned in route settings
- define fallback target (quantized model / smaller arch)
- set SLI thresholds and alert destinations
- configure tracing hook and sampling rate (10%)
- run a simulated traffic spike (2–3x expected) and record results
- capture failure reproduction steps in Jira linked to pilot ticket

Telemetry queries (short, for SE to paste into console):
- "Avg token latency by model over last 24h"
- "Top 10 routes by cost this week"
- "5xx rate by region last 7d"
(we'll add exact query syntax to the SE cheat-sheet)

Pricing nudges to use in-conversation:
- "If your steady-state is predictable, our Dedicated commitment reduces unit cost by ~20–40% versus on-demand hosted for the same SLO — we can model your projected spend during the pilot."
- "We can also run burst policies to handle episodic peak traffic without over-provisioning permanently."

Competitive framing (brief):
- Cloud LLM endpoints: Compete on unified migration path + observability and fallback granularity.
- Open-source self-hosted stacks: Compete on time-to-reliability and ongoing ops overhead reduction.

Playbook appendix (practical notes and TODOs):
- Add SRE-approved canary runbook link (TODO: Liam)
- Attach Dedicated pricing sheet for quick quote (TODO: Priya)
- Create a short one-pager for Security leads summarizing KMS/HSM and audit logs (TODO: Samir)

Open questions for product/R&D (to surface during weekly sync):
- Can we expose a pre-populated telemetry card for "pilot summary" in console? (would reduce demo setup time)
- Can Optimize return a single recommended quantization profile for a given prompt set (paired with estimated BLEU/quality delta)?

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep this doc intentionally lightweight: sellers want a one-pager + two quick scripts.
- Build a 2-slide "pilot checklist" slide that SEs can brand when working deals.
- Follow up with platform-ops team to add a 1-click export of pilot metrics into a CSV for buyer reviews.

End of draft — this is a working file. Add suggested language back to the SE pocket-card and iterate after first ten pilots.
